note: Research snapshot of pending Australian AI regulatory developments. Every item is a watch item, not an obligation. Confirm each against its primary source at use time; policai.org is a discovery index only.

watch_items.item: Legislated 'Australian Standards for AI' and Office of AI
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Announced 15 July 2026; Office of AI established in PM&C; legislation targeted early 2027; confirmed scope so far limited to large-AI-data-centre requirements and creator-consent copyright protections; National Cabinet outcome not yet published at the snapshot (the 26 August 2026 communique is now on pm.gov.au)
watch_items.expected_trigger: PM&C consultation outcome, exposure draft or Bill introduction (targeted early 2027)
watch_items.status_at_review: Confirmed: National Cabinet met on 26 August 2026 and agreed the Commonwealth will work with the States and Territories to develop nationally consistent mandatory standards for large data centres (energy, water, land use), with the Commonwealth intending to legislate in early 2027; commentary (not the communique) reports that a renewables requirement was not agreed. PM&C then opened the consultation 'Getting it right: Building AI infrastructure that works for Australia' (18 September to 9 October 2026), which also covers conditions for training AI models and support for copyright holders. Separately, a reported (leaked) Attorney-General's Department paper floats an opt-out model for AI training, so the copyright limb should be treated as under consultation, not as settled creator-consent protection
watch_items.review_basis: National Cabinet communique and PM&C consultation page read on 24 Sep 2026; the opt-out copyright paper rests on secondary sources

Numbering note: the commencing amendment inserts APP 1.7–1.9 (the snapshot text's 'APP 1.7-1.8' is a numbering slip), commencing 10 December 2026

watch_items.item: Second tranche of Privacy Act reform
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Government commitment only; Attorney-General confirmed in February 2026 Senate estimates that a tranche 2 Bill is being progressed; no Bill introduced, no timetable
watch_items.status_at_review: Reported: on 31 August 2026 the Attorney-General's Department released an exposure draft Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026 and consultation paper; submissions closed 18 September 2026. Reported proposals include a fair-and-reasonable test, an expanded personal-information definition, a 72-hour Commissioner notification for eligible data breaches and a right to erasure against large digital platforms; removal of the small-business and employee-records exemptions is reportedly not included; the commencement table is reportedly blank. An exposure draft is not a Bill and not law
watch_items.review_basis: official consultation page seen in search results only, plus secondary sources; confirm against the primary source before relying on it
